newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner, Turner warn of layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner, Turner warn of layoffs.

text.p: The joint Time Warner and Turner Broadcasting System merger steering committee told the companies' more than 70,000 employees in an internal memo Thursday they can expect layoffs in "overlap" areas now that the merger is complete.
The committee, however, gave no indication of numbers or of which specific divisions would be targeted.
However, the memo maintained that employees in Turner's news and entertainment networks will not "generally" be affected.

"It is our plan to leave the operations of the networks intact and in Atlanta, and to consolidate non-network functions in New York and Los Angeles," the memo said. "We have no headcount number. What we are trying to achieve is an organization without unnecessary duplication."

The memo, along with an additional note from Turner chairman Ted Turner and Time Warner chairman Jerry Levin, was distributed the same day the Federal Trade Commission formally approved the corporate marriage between the firms. On Wall Street, Time Warner's stock price closed up $2 to $37.
Reports have been circulating for several weeks that Turner would lay off between 500 and 1,000 of its 8,000 employees.

Sources pointed to a number of Turner divisions that will either be downsized or eliminated in the merger, including homevideo, licensing and merchandising, publishing, accounting, business affairs, legal and investor relations.
A TBS representative would not confirm those areas.

The memo added that a hiring freeze was in effect at Turner and in selected areas at Time Warner to "ensure" that laid off employees would have a shot at being slotted in other posts. It also promised severance benefits and outplacement assistance to laid off workers.
